title: Ordinary etale smooth purity with diagonal normalization
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and $p:P\to X$ a smooth separated compactifiable morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On ordinary small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use the right adjoint $p^!$ of ordinary $Rp_!$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. With $\Lambda(1)=\mu_\ell\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell}\Lambda$, signed tensor powers as in [def-per-potential-dualizing], and $M(d)=M\otimes^L\Lambda(d)$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], there are natural isomorphisms
$$\gamma_{p,M}:p^*M(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}p^!M\qquad(M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)).$$
They commute with restriction to etale open charts, Noetherian change of base, and composition of smooth morphisms under the compact-support right-adjoint transitivity comparison. Their normalization is the diagonal-class orientation: on the affine line the first Chern class of the diagonal defines the duality unit and integration sends the Kummer first Chern class of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(1)$ to $1$; the deformation to the normal cone identifies the resulting dualizing line with the roots-of-unity Tate line. On affine $d$-space the orientation is the ordered tensor product of these affine-line orientations. For $d=0$ it is the etale inverse-image comparison. No perfect-field or finite-field hypothesis is imposed.
